reviews.summary: Asked to drop the Hallmark citation (VOICE.md: don't name other gift makers outside comparison posts), to say 'the moment they wake up' rather than 'you', and to word the free-note line so photos don't read as free. Polish: 'staying in', 'a sentence or two' per part, possible 5th-year row.

Museum note promised a year per plaque, but the template prints one shared 'years' field under each caption; 'you wake up' should be 'they'; the 10th and 40th milestone lines repeated earlier lines ('I'd ... again', 'make it look easy'); 'pricing up' is British; Spanish calques ('cómo se sienten', 'Cambia a tus padres', 'Con una a tres frases', 'mis cantos'); the back-link sentence in anniversary-letter-to-boyfriend made the eighty-word letter read as one of the 'shorter ones'.
Asked for husband/wife in the partner heading and in the line under it, since the top results and searchers use those words. Polish: shorter description, 5th/30th rows, a faith-based line.

reviews.summary: All three round-1 fixes made. The searcher gets a three-part formula and a finished sample card on the first screen, then lines by recipient, tone, year and hard year, a length table, signing advice and what to leave out, which is more than a page of stock quotes, with the product only at the end. Polish: 'a couple you're not part of' in the lead; an optional 5th-year row.

Every round-1 fix made correctly in both languages; every product and template claim matches manifest, schema, Template.tsx, extras.tsx and messages, every link resolves, and the Spanish reads as written in Spain, section by section the same post. Polish: 'your parents' anniversary' in the Museum note; small Spanish smoothings in the lead, the 60th line and an FAQ answer; 'the days the car broke down'.

Both round-1 fixes made; it answers every People-also-ask question and beats the Hallmark, Grammarly, Shutterfly and American Greetings pages with a formula, worked examples, length by recipient, how to sign and what to leave out, where they mostly list stock lines.
